About Midjourney

Midjourney, Inc. is a self-described independent research lab. It sells subscription access, at about $10–$120 a month, to a text-to-image and video generation service. The service runs on a web app and Discord. David Holz founded it in 2021, and it has taken no outside funding. Press estimates put revenue at around $500M a year (2025–2026), but the company publishes no audited figures. Its V8.2 model was released in July 2026, and headcount is estimated at about 100–165.

Aggregator estimate (~$500M gross run rate, Clink/Presenc); last outlet-confirmed figure is ~$300M fiscal 2024 revenue (Forbes citing PitchBook) and Holz's 'well above $200M' to The Information. No priced round exists, so the $5B valuation is an estimate; Forbes put headcount at ~60 in Apr 2026 (not company-confirmed). Unchanged.

- 7 August 2026: Substantially corrected. The previous version of this article was titled "Midjourney Makes $500M a Year With 40 People and $0 Raised" and built its central argument on $12.5M of revenue per employee. Midjourney has never published a headcount; current public estimates range from about 40 to 163 people, which makes any per-employee figure unusable. We removed the calculation, the headcount claim in the title and headline, and the derived profit figure of "$350-400M". We also removed a subscriber claim, "16 million paying users at roughly $31 per month", that implied nearly $6B in annual revenue and therefore contradicted this article's own revenue figure by an order of magnitude. Revenue is now given as the $300M-$500M range, profitability as reported rather than calculated. Sector-wide comparisons moved to the AI revenue leaderboard so the figures live in one place instead of ageing separately in several.
